title: Lucy Simpson:
title_q: “Safety Is Not the Absence of Violence”
title_short: Lucy Simpson · Safety Is Not the Absence of Violence
headline: The CEO explains, in one breath, why NIWRC's idea of safety is bigger than the absence of violence: housing, income, health, culture, and Native women leading it.
story: Lucy Simpson is the Chief Executive Officer of NIWRC. On the patio at SkyDance Brewing, before the reception, she gave the clearest version of the safety framework we have on camera. This cut is that definition, said plainly, ending on who leads the work: Native women.

Loops: L1 “If safety is not the absence of violence, what is it?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:03 (“all of the conditions that are required”). L2 “Who makes that safety real?” opens at 0:00 and closes in the BUTTON (“Native women leadership really is the foundation of this work”). Stakes: high rates of violence in Native communities, from a history of colonization, and the people doing the work on the ground every day.
do: Open on Lucy mid-sentence with the hook text on frame 1.
Let her finish each thought. Cut on breaths, not mid-word.
Use C1 for sound. Use C1 or C2 for picture.
Say “Native women-led” out loud on screen: it is in her button line.
Use only the files named here.
dont: No logo, name or fade at 0:00.
No stock footage. No images of harm or fear. No red handprint.
No Tribal affiliation on the name super. Name and title only.
Do not cut the list (housing, economic security, health) short. The list is the point.
No somber grade. Keep it bright.

voice.quote: and for us at NIWRC safety is the all of the conditions that are required to ensure that our Native women families and communities can live their lives with dignity and with protection and that our Native communities can can exercise their full sovereignty.

rows.frame_alt: Lucy, hand open, counting the conditions.
rows.visual: Lucy on camera 01:20.2 on. If the B-roll has a quiet wide of the room or the patio, 2 seconds of it is fine under the list. B-roll TBD on scrub.
rows.motion: Key words on screen as she says them, one at a time: <q>housing</q> · <q>economic security</q> · <q>health</q>. Small, lower third of the frame.

voice.quote: So it means having conditions like safe and affordable housing available for community members. It means economic security and opportunities for for growth in that area. It means having health access, the ability to promote wellness. All of those things are what we need in our communities to be safe.

rows.visual: Lucy on camera 03:01.2 on. Stakes land here.

voice.quote: Working to promote and advance safety in Native communities is so important right now because we do have such high rates of violence within our communities. … All of these things are from that history of colonization and the way it's impacted our communities ongoing

rows.visual: Lucy on camera 03:57.1 on. B-roll of guests arriving or talking is fine for 2 to 3 seconds here (B1 clips, TBD on scrub). Dignity only: people talking, laughing, listening.

voice.quote: Supporting Native-led advocacy, what it does is it provides the opportunity for the voices of survivors to be centered in this work

rows.frame_alt: Lucy, chin up, delivering the leadership line.
rows.visual: Lucy on camera 06:14.7 on. Hold one second on her face after “tribal leaders”. Loop 2 closes here.
rows.motion: Captions only. Key words: <q>Native women</q>, <q>foundation</q>, <q>tribal leaders</q>.

voice.quote: Native women leadership really is the foundation of this work to promote safety in our Native communities. Native women form the backbone of our communities. They are life-givers, they are teaching our children, they are working in the workforce and they are tribal leaders.
